title: Marconi's first wireless signals beyond the hill at Villa Griffone
summary: In the summer of 1895 Guglielmo Marconi sent radiotelegraphic signals from the garden of his family's Villa Griffone at Pontecchio to a receiver beyond the Celestini hill, about two kilometres away, past an obstacle in the way. Reception was signalled back by a gunshot. The IEEE regards the experiment as the start of wireless communication.

uncertainty.note: The IEEE page gives the summer of 1895 without a day; the Nobel Prize biography gives 1895 for the start of his experiments at Pontecchio.

where.modern_name: Villa Griffone, Pontecchio Marconi, Sasso Marconi, Italy
where.historical_name: Villa Griffone, the Marconi family home at Pontecchio, Kingdom of Italy

importance.justification: Early demonstration of radiotelegraphy past an obstacle, regarded by the IEEE as the start of wireless communication.

sources.title: Milestones: Marconi's Early Experiments in Wireless Telegraphy, 1895

reviewer_note: Distances differ: the IEEE says about two kilometres, the Nobel biography one and a half miles (about 2.4 km); the summary uses the IEEE figure. The Nobel page names the family estate at Pontecchio but not Villa Griffone; the IEEE page ties the garden to Villa Griffone.
